```markdown
# Batch tracking design

Date: 2026-10-28
Status: Agreed in design session. Ready for an implementation plan.

## Goal

Trace any bottle back to its batch. Trace the batch back to the lot number of every malt and hop sack that went into it.

## Scope

In scope:
- Batches, from mash day to bottling.
- Ingredient sacks (malt and hops) and their supplier lot numbers.
- Recording which sacks went into which batch.
- Bottling runs and the labels they print.
- A trace lookup in both directions: bottle to sacks, and sack to batches.

Out of scope:
- Inventory and stock levels.
- Taproom tabs. The existing tab code does not change.

## Where it runs

The feature is part of the existing Flask app on the office Raspberry Pi. It uses the same SQLite database. It needs no new server and no network service.

## Workflow

1. **Mash day.** A brewer starts a batch. The app gives it a batch number.
2. **Sack opened.** The brewer scans the sack's lot number. The app links that lot to the open batch. Nobody types the lot number, because the brewers' hands are usually wet.
3. **Bottling.** The brewer starts a bottling run for the batch. Each label gets the batch number and the bottling date. The label printer prints them.
4. **Trace.** Anyone can enter a batch number from a bottle. The app shows the batch and every lot number that went into it.

## Data model

| Table | Purpose | Key fields |
|---|---|---|
| `batches` | One row for each batch | `id`, `batch_number` (unique), `mash_date`, `status` |
| `lots` | One row for each supplier lot | `id`, `lot_number` (unique), `ingredient_type` (malt or hop), `supplier` |
| `batch_lots` | Links a lot to a batch when a sack is scanned | `batch_id`, `lot_id`, `scanned_at` |
| `bottling_runs` | One row for each bottling run | `id`, `batch_id`, `bottling_date`, `label_count` |

The `batch_lots` table makes the link many-to-many. One batch uses many lots. One lot can feed many batches.

Trace records are append-only. A wrong scan is marked as void with a reason. It is not deleted, so the history stays complete for a recall.

## Scanning

A USB barcode scanner acts as a keyboard. It types the code and presses Enter. The scan page is one large input field that keeps focus. The page needs no special driver.

If a scanned lot number is new, the app asks for the ingredient type and supplier one time. After that, the same lot scans without questions.

## Labels

The app sends the batch number and bottling date to the label printer. The printer model and its print interface are not known yet. They must be confirmed before implementation.

## Assumptions to confirm during implementation

These items did not come up in the session. The design works with the default shown here.

- **Batch number format.** Default: year and a sequence number, for example `2026-014`.
- **Sacks used across batches.** A sack scanned only when opened links only to the first batch. Default: the brewer scans a sack again in each batch that uses it.
- **Backups.** The trace records live on one SD card. Default: a nightly copy of the SQLite file to a second device.

## Next step

Write the implementation plan from this design.
```

Here is the design: `docs/plans/2026-10-28-batch-tracking-design.md`. It covers the four parts we agreed on: batches, sack lots, scanning on open, and bottling labels.

I made the technical choices myself, as you asked. The feature goes into the existing Flask app and SQLite database on the Pi. It does not need a new server.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The link table `batch_lots` is the core of traceability. It answers "what went into this bottle?" and the reverse recall question "which batches used this bad lot?"
- Most USB barcode scanners act as a keyboard. The scan page is a plain input field, and it needs no driver code on the Pi.
- Trace records are never deleted, only marked as void. In a recall, a gap in the history is worse than a wrong scan with a correction note.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The doc has three short assumptions at the end, each with a default, so they do not block anything. One of them matters for traceability. If a sack is opened in one batch and finished in the next, a scan only at opening misses the second batch. My default is to scan the sack again each time it is used.

I do not know the label printer model. That is the one fact the build needs from you.

Next, I can write the implementation plan from this doc.
